summary: Work completed 14 experiments in 314.1 minutes, with 4 classified as compute-bound. The bounded slowest list contains only synthesis work, so it cannot rank the compute-bound experiments or explain their runtime; the locked task-conditioned GPU-idle value is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The bounded slowest set is entirely synthesis-only and is led by the transition-evidence task; the supplied data does not isolate the slow phase within that work.
Disk-mtime reconstruction supplies aggregate durations but not phase-level timing, leaving the compute-bound ranking and causal attribution unavailable.
The supplied evidence does not correlate model concurrency, runner selection, or GPU telemetry with individual compute-bound tasks.
improvements_suggested: Add resumable, content-addressed checkpoints to long synthesis workflows so unchanged transition, ingestion, and reconciliation inputs can be reused.
Emit per-phase start and stop receipts plus task-correlated GPU utilization in each experiment artifact.
Declare model concurrency in the task manifest and select DualGPURunner only for concurrent multi-model execution.
Use dependency-aware scheduling to start ready independent tasks without waiting for unrelated synthesis work.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Make long synthesis workflows incremental and resumable.
Replace reconstruction-only timing with per-phase, task-correlated timing and GPU receipts.
Add manifest-driven concurrency and runner selection, with DualGPURunner reserved for concurrent multi-model tasks.
meta_reflection: The visible long tail belongs to synthesis-only work, while the bounded evidence omits the compute-bound names, durations, and phase causes needed for a hardware diagnosis. Improving synthesis reuse and task-level observability is justified; stronger GPU or runner claims are not.
